fields.name: I
fields.text: Global interrupt switch: while 0 no interrupt runs whatever the separate enables say; hardware clears it when an interrupt is taken and RETI sets it again; SEI and CLI set and clear it from software.

fields.name: T
fields.text: One-bit holding place for bit copies: BST loads it from a bit of a working register and BLD writes it back into a bit of one.

fields.name: H
fields.text: Half carry flag: set on a half carry in some arithmetic operations; useful in BCD arithmetic.

fields.name: S
fields.text: Sign bit: always N exclusive-OR V.

fields.name: V
fields.text: Two's complement overflow flag, used in two's complement arithmetic.

fields.name: N
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic result is negative.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic result is zero.

fields.name: C
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic operation produces a carry.

registers.name: EEARH
registers.title: EEPROM Address Register
notes: Initial value of bit 0 printed as X/0.

fields.name: EEAR8
fields.text: Top EEPROM address bit, used on ATtiny861A; on ATtiny261A and ATtiny461A it is reserved and reads 0. EEAR starts undefined, so load an address before any EEPROM access.

registers.name: EEARL
registers.title: EEPROM Address Register
notes: Initial value of bit 7 printed as X/0.

fields.name: EEAR7
fields.text: EEPROM address bit 7, the top address bit on ATtiny461A; on ATtiny261A it is reserved and reads 0. EEAR starts undefined, so load an address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: Low EEPROM address bits; EEPROM bytes are addressed linearly from 0 up to 128/256/512. EEAR starts undefined, so load an address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: EEPROM data byte: holds the byte to be written to the EEAR address on a write, and receives the byte from the EEAR address on a read.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: Chooses what a write of EEPE does: erase and write together in one atomic operation, erase only, or write only. Writes to EEPM are ignored while EEPE is 1. Reset returns it to 0b00 unless an EEPROM programming operation is under way.

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: 1 enables the EEPROM Ready interrupt, provided SREG.I is 1; 0 disables it. The interrupt keeps firing for as long as the non-volatile memory is ready to be programmed.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: Arms EEPE: with EEMPE at 1, setting EEPE within four clock cycles programs the EEPROM at the chosen address; with EEMPE at 0, setting EEPE does nothing. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after software writes it to 1.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: Starts EEPROM programming as EEPM selects; it only takes effect if EEMPE was written to 1 first. Hardware clears it once the write time has passed. Setting it stalls the CPU for two cycles before the next instruction.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: Read strobe: with the address in EEAR, write 1 to read the EEPROM; the data is ready at once, the read takes one instruction and the CPU stalls four cycles before the next. Poll EEPE first: during a write neither a read nor a change of EEAR is possible.

fields.name: GPIOR2
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 2.

fields.name: GPIOR1
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 1.

fields.name: GPIOR0
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 0.

registers.name: OSCCAL
registers.title: Oscillator Calibration Register
notes: Initial value of bits 7:0 printed as Device Specific Calibration Value.

fields.name: CAL
fields.text: Trims the calibrated internal oscillator against process variation; a factory value is loaded at chip reset and software may write another. 0x00 is the lowest frequency, 0xFF the highest; calibration outside the specified range is not guaranteed. This oscillator also times EEPROM and Flash writes, so their write times shift with it; when writing EEPROM or Flash, keep it at or below 8.8 MHz, or the write may fail.

registers.name: CLKPR
registers.title: Clock Prescale Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Unlocks CLKPS: write 1 while writing 0 to every other bit of CLKPR. Hardware clears it four cycles later or when CLKPS is written; writing it again inside that window neither restarts nor clears the window.

fields.name: CLKPS
fields.text: Divider from the selected clock source to the system clock, changeable at run time; all synchronous peripherals slow by the same factor. To change it, write CLKPCE to 1 with the other bits 0, then within four cycles write the new CLKPS with CLKPCE at 0, with interrupts disabled. Reset value follows the CKDIV8 fuse: 0000 when unprogrammed, 0011 (divide by 8) when programmed; any value may be written whatever the fuse. Parts ship with CKDIV8 programmed.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: BOD Sleep: 1 turns the BOD off in the sleep mode entered next. Timed write: set BODS and BODSE both to 1, then within four clock cycles write BODS 1 with BODSE 0. It becomes active three clock cycles after being set and clears itself three clock cycles later, so SLEEP must run in that time.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up Disable.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep Enable: must be 1 for the SLEEP instruction to put the MCU to sleep. Setting it just before SLEEP and clearing it right after wake-up keeps the MCU from entering sleep unintended.

fields.name: SM
fields.text: Picks which of the four sleep modes SLEEP enters.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: BOD Sleep Enable: allows BODS to be set, as part of the timed sequence that turns the BOD off in sleep.

fields.name: ISC01
fields.text: Interrupt Sense Control 0 bit 1.

fields.name: ISC00
fields.text: Interrupt Sense Control 0 bit 0.

fields.name: PRTIM1
fields.text: 1 stops Timer/Counter1; once it is enabled again it carries on as it was before the stop.

fields.name: PRTIM0
fields.text: 1 stops Timer/Counter0; once it is enabled again it carries on as it was before the stop.

fields.name: PRUSI
fields.text: 1 stops the USI by gating off its clock; reinitialise the USI after waking it again.

fields.name: PRADC
fields.text: 1 stops the ADC, which must be disabled first. The analog comparator also uses this clock.

registers.name: MCUSR
registers.title: MCU Status Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Set by a Watchdog reset; a Power-on reset clears it, as does a write of 0.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Set by a Brown-out reset; a Power-on reset clears it, as does a write of 0.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: Set by an External reset; a Power-on reset clears it, as does a write of 0.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Set by a Power-on reset; cleared only by writing 0 to it. Reading and then clearing MCUSR early in the program lets the flags show the source of the next reset.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Set on a Watchdog time-out when the Watchdog is set up for interrupt. Cleared by hardware when its interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1 to it. With SREG.I and WDIE at 1 the time-out interrupt runs.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: With WDIE 1, WDE 0 and SREG.I 1, a Watchdog time-out raises an interrupt instead of a reset. If WDE is 1, hardware clears WDIE at a time-out, so the next time-out resets the part unless WDIE is set again after each interrupt.

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 3; WDP[3:0] set the Watchdog time-out while the Watchdog is enabled. A reserved setting at or above 0b1010 falls back to one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Must be 1 when WDE is written to 0, or the Watchdog stays enabled; also required to change the prescaler bits. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: 1 enables the Watchdog Timer, 0 disables it; it can be cleared only while WDCE is 1. To disable: write 1 to both WDCE and WDE in one write (WDE 1 even if already 1), then within four clock cycles write WDE 0. In safety level 2 the Watchdog cannot be disabled. In safety level 1 WDRF in MCUSR forces WDE to 1, so WDRF must be cleared before the disable sequence. When the Watchdog is unused, clear WDRF and WDE during initialisation: an accidental enable would otherwise bring repeated Watchdog resets.

fields.name: WDP2
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 2; WDP[3:0] set the Watchdog time-out while the Watchdog is enabled. A reserved setting at or above 0b1010 falls back to one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDP1
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 1; WDP[3:0] set the Watchdog time-out while the Watchdog is enabled. A reserved setting at or above 0b1010 falls back to one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDP0
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 0; WDP[3:0] set the Watchdog time-out while the Watchdog is enabled. A reserved setting at or above 0b1010 falls back to one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.text: BOD Sleep.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up Disable.

fields.text: Sleep Mode select bit 1.

fields.name: SM0
fields.text: Sleep Mode select bit 0.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: BOD Sleep Enable.

fields.name: ISC0
fields.text: Selects the level or edge on INT0 or INT1 that raises External Interrupt 0, which fires when SREG.I and its mask are set. The pin is sampled before edge detection: in edge or toggle modes a pulse longer than one clock period always raises it, a shorter one may not; in low-level mode the level must last until the current instruction completes.

values.text: Low level on INT0 or INT1.
Any logic change on INT0 or INT1.
Falling edge on INT0 or INT1.
Rising edge on INT0 or INT1.

fields.name: INT1
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the INT1 external pin interrupt; ISC01 and ISC00 in MCUCR choose edge or level. Activity on the pin requests the interrupt even when INT1 is an output. It runs from the INT1 vector.

fields.name: INT0
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the INT0 external pin interrupt; ISC01 and ISC00 in MCUCR choose edge or level. Activity on the pin requests the interrupt even when INT0 is an output. It runs from the INT0 vector.

fields.name: PCIE1
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, a change on any PCINT[7:0] or PCINT[15:12] pin enabled in PCMSK0 or PCMSK1 raises the pin change interrupt, which runs from the PCI vector.

fields.name: PCIE0
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, a change on any PCINT[11:8] pin enabled in PCMSK1 raises the pin change interrupt, which runs from the PCI vector.

registers.name: GIFR
registers.title: General Interrupt Flag Register
notes: The register summary prints bit 7 as INTF1.

fields.name: INT1
fields.text: External Interrupt Flag 1: set when an edge or logic change on INT1 requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and GIMSK.INT1 at 1 the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the handler runs or by writing 1 to it; always 0 while INT1 is set to level sensing.

fields.name: INTF0
fields.text: Set when an edge or logic change on INT0 requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and GIMSK.INT0 at 1 the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the handler runs or by writing 1 to it; always 0 while INT0 is set to level sensing.

fields.name: PCIF
fields.text: Set when a logic change on an enabled PCINT pin requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and the GIMSK pin change enable at 1 the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the handler runs or by writing 1 to it.

fields.name: PCINT
fields.text: One bit per pin PCINT0 to PCINT7: 1 enables the pin change interrupt on that pin, provided GIMSK.PCIE1 is 1; 0 disables it.

fields.name: PCINT[15:8]
fields.text: One bit per pin PCINT8 to PCINT15: 1 enables the pin change interrupt on that pin, gated by GIMSK.PCIE0 for PCINT[11:8] and by GIMSK.PCIE1 for PCINT[15:12]; 0 disables it.

fields.name: TCW0
fields.text: 1 puts Timer/Counter0 in 16-bit mode: the counter becomes 16 bits wide and OCR0A and OCR0B join as one 16-bit compare register. TCNT0H/L and OCR0B/A then need the special 16-bit access procedure, since the CPU reaches them over the 8-bit bus.

fields.name: ICEN0
fields.text: 1 enables Input Capture mode.

fields.name: ICNC0
fields.text: 1 turns on the noise filter on the ICP0 input: the input changes only after four successive equal samples, which delays the capture by four system clock cycles.

fields.name: ICES0
fields.text: Chooses the ICP0 edge that triggers a capture: 0 falling, 1 rising. On a capture the counter value goes into the Input Capture Register and ICF0 is set, which can raise the Input Capture interrupt if enabled.

fields.name: ACIC0
fields.text: 1 lets the Analog Comparator output trigger the Timer/Counter0 input capture, through its noise canceler and edge select; 0 leaves them unconnected. TIMSK.TICIE0 must be set for the comparator to raise the capture interrupt.

fields.name: CTC0
fields.text: Sets the counting sequence and the source of TOP: Normal mode or Clear Timer on Compare Match (CTC) mode.

registers.name: TCCR0B
registers.title: Timer/Counter0 Control Register B
notes: The bit diagram prints bit 0 as CS01; the register summary's CS00 is carried.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: 1 starts synchronization mode: the value written to PSR0 is held, keeping the prescaler in reset so the timer stays halted while being set up. Writing 0 lets hardware clear PSR0 and the timer starts counting.

fields.name: PSR0
fields.text: 1 resets the Timer/Counter0 prescaler. Hardware clears it at once unless TSM is 1.

fields.name: CS0
fields.text: Chooses the Timer/Counter0 clock source and prescale. With an external T0 setting, edges on pin T0 clock the counter even when the pin is an output, so software can drive the count.

values.text: External clock on pin T0, falling edge.
External clock on pin T0, rising edge.

fields.name: TCNT0L
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 count, low byte.

fields.name: TCNT0H
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 count, high byte.

fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Output Compare Register A.

fields.name: OCR0B
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Output Compare Register B.

fields.name: OCIE1D
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Match D Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE1A
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Match A Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE1B
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Match B Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE0A
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the Timer/Counter0 Compare Match A interrupt, which runs when OCF0A is set.

fields.name: OCIE0B
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the Timer/Counter0 Compare Match B interrupt, which runs when OCF0B is set.

fields.name: TOIE1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Overflow Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: TOIE0
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the Timer/Counter0 Overflow interrupt, which runs when TOV0 is set.

fields.name: TICIE0
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the Input Capture interrupt, whose vector runs when ICF0 in TIFR is set.

fields.name: OCF1D
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 1D.

fields.name: OCF1A
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 1A.

fields.name: OCF1B
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 1B.

fields.name: OCF0A
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter0 and OCR0A, and in 16-bit mode on a match against OCR0B/A; not set in Input Capture mode while OCR0A serves as capture register. Cleared when its vector runs or by writing 1 to it. With SREG.I and OCIE0A at 1 the compare match interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF0B
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter0 and OCR0B; not set when OCR0B serves as the high byte of the 16-bit compare or capture register. Cleared when its vector runs or by writing 1 to it. With SREG.I and OCIE0B at 1 the compare match interrupt runs.

fields.name: TOV1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Overflow Flag.

fields.name: TOV0
fields.text: Set when Timer/Counter0 overflows. Cleared when its vector runs or by writing 1 to it. With SREG.I and TOIE0 at 1 the overflow interrupt runs.

fields.name: ICF0
fields.text: Set by a capture event on ICP0, or, when ICR0 is used as TOP, when the counter reaches TOP. Cleared when the Input Capture vector runs or by writing 1 to it.

fields.name: COM1A
fields.text: Sets how compare match A drives the waveform output OCW1A and whether pin OC1A is connected; any nonzero setting takes the pin over from the port, and in PWM modes setting 01 also connects the inverted output. The pin's DDR bit must be 1 for the driver to work. The effect depends on PWM1A and WGM1[1:0]. Mirrored by COM1A1S and COM1A0S in TCCR1C: writing either copy changes the other.

fields.name: FPEN1

fields.name: FPNC1

fields.name: FPES1

fields.name: FPAC1
fields.text: 1 lets the Analog Comparator output trigger Timer/Counter1 Fault Protection, through its noise canceler and edge select; 0 leaves them unconnected. FPIE1 must be set for the comparator to raise the fault interrupt.

fields.name: FPF1
fields.text: Fault Protection interrupt flag: the fault interrupt runs from its vector when SREG.I, FPIE1 and FPF1 are 1; pin activity requests it even when the fault pin is an output. Cleared when its vector runs, or a synchronization clock cycle after a write of 1.

fields.name: WGM1
fields.text: With PWM1A/PWM1B, choose the Timer/Counter1 counting sequence and waveform: Normal, Fast PWM, Phase and Frequency Correct PWM, or PWM6.

fields.name: OC1OE
fields.text: One bit per Output Compare pin in PWM6 modes: 1 connects the pin to the waveform, taking effect at once; 0 disconnects it and the pin shows the port register value.

registers.name: PLLCSR
registers.title: PLL Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 1 printed as 0/1.

fields.name: LSM
fields.text: 1 selects Low Speed mode, which scales the fast peripheral clock down to 32 MHz; required below 2.7 V supply, since Timer/Counter1 is too slow at low voltage. Timer/Counter1 is best stopped whenever LSM changes. Cannot be set while PLLCLK is the system clock.

fields.name: PCKE
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 clock choice: 1 selects asynchronous mode on the fast PCK clock (64 MHz, or 32 MHz in Low Speed mode); 0 selects synchronous mode on the system clock CK. Can be set only once the PLL is enabled (CKSEL fuse set to PLL clock, or PLLE 1), and safely only when PLOCK is 1.

fields.name: PLLE
fields.text: 1 starts the PLL, and the internal oscillator as its reference if needed. Always 1 when the PLL is the system clock source.

fields.name: PLOCK
fields.text: 1 when the PLL is locked to its reference. Ignore it during the initial lock-in while the frequency over- and undershoots; steady state comes within 100 µs. After lock-in, check it before enabling PCK for Timer/Counter1.

fields.name: TCNT1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count, low byte.

fields.name: TC1[9:8]
fields.text: Holds the top two bits, TC19 and TC18, during 10-bit accesses; one TC1H serves every 10-bit register of Timer/Counter1. Access to the 10-bit TCNT1 over the 8-bit bus needs the special procedure.

fields.name: OCR1A
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Register A.

fields.name: OCR1B
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Register B.

fields.name: OCR1C
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Register C.

fields.name: OCR1D
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Register D.

fields.name: OCIE1D
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the Timer/Counter1 Compare Match D interrupt, at vector $010, which runs on a compare match D; the match sets its flag in TIFR.

fields.name: OCIE1A
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the Timer/Counter1 Compare Match A interrupt, at vector $003, which runs on a compare match A; the match sets its flag in TIFR.

fields.name: OCIE1B
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the Timer/Counter1 Compare Match B interrupt, at vector $009, which runs on a compare match B; the match sets its flag in TIFR.

fields.name: OCIE0A
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Output Compare Match A Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE0B
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Output Compare Match B Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: TOIE1
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, enables the Timer/Counter1 Overflow interrupt, at vector $004, which runs when Timer/Counter1 overflows; the overflow sets TOV1 in TIFR.

fields.name: TOIE0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Overflow Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: TICIE0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Input Capture Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCF1D
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter1 and OCR1D. Cleared when its vector runs, or a synchronization clock cycle after a write of 1. With SREG.I and OCIE1D at 1 the compare match D interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF1A
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter1 and OCR1A. Cleared when its vector runs, or a synchronization clock cycle after a write of 1. With SREG.I and OCIE1A at 1 the compare match A interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF1B
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter1 and OCR1B. Cleared when its vector runs, or a synchronization clock cycle after a write of 1. With SREG.I and OCIE1B at 1 the compare match B interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF0A
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 0A.

fields.name: OCF0B
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 0B.

fields.name: TOV1
fields.text: Overflow flag. Normal and Fast PWM modes: set when the counter reaches TOP, in the cycle it resets to BOTTOM. Phase and Frequency Correct PWM: set when the counter reaches BOTTOM. Cleared when its vector runs, or a synchronization clock cycle after a write of 1. With SREG.I and TOIE1 at 1 the overflow interrupt runs.

fields.name: TOV0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Overflow Flag.

fields.name: ICF0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Input Capture Flag.

fields.name: DT1H
fields.text: Dead time for the OC1x output, counted in prescaled timer clocks: from 0 up to 15 prescaled clock periods.

fields.name: DT1L
fields.text: Dead time for the complementary OC1x output, counted in prescaled timer clocks: from 0 up to 15 prescaled clock periods.

fields.name: USIDR
fields.text: USI Data Register.

fields.name: USIBR
fields.text: USI Buffer Register.

fields.name: USISIF
fields.text: Two-wire mode: set on a start condition. Output-disable or three-wire mode with USICS 0b11 or 0b10 and USICLK 0: set by any SCK edge. Raises an interrupt when USISIE and the global enable are 1, which wakes the CPU from every sleep mode. Cleared only by writing 1 to it, which also releases the start-detect hold of USCL in two-wire mode.

fields.name: USIOIF
fields.text: Set when the 4-bit counter rolls over from 15 to 0. Raises an interrupt when USIOIE and the global enable are 1, which wakes the CPU from Idle. Cleared only by writing 1 to it, which in two-wire mode also lets go of SCL held low by the overflow.

fields.name: USIPF
fields.text: Two-wire mode: set on a stop condition; cleared by writing 1 to it. Raises no interrupt. Useful for two-wire bus master arbitration.

fields.name: USIDC
fields.text: 1 when bit 7 of USIDR does not match the pin's level; meaningful only in two-wire mode. Useful for two-wire bus master arbitration.

fields.name: USICNT
fields.text: The 4-bit counter, readable and writable. It counts up once per clock from the external edge detector, a Timer/Counter0 compare match, or the USICLK or USITC strobes, as USICS[1:0] select. With an external source (USICS1 1), writing USICLK 1 lets USITC writes clock it. The external clock input USCK/SCL can drive the counter even with USIWM[1:0] = 0.

fields.name: USISIE
fields.text: 1 enables the start condition interrupt; a pending one runs as soon as this bit and the global enable are both 1.

fields.name: USIOIE
fields.text: 1 enables the counter overflow interrupt; a pending one runs as soon as this bit and the global enable are both 1.

fields.name: USIWM
fields.text: Wire mode: changes only how the outputs behave. Data and clock inputs work the same in every mode, so the counter and USIDR can be clocked externally and data sampled with the outputs disabled. In two-wire modes DI and USCK act as SDA and SCL.

values.text: Outputs, clock hold and start detector off; the pins work as ordinary port pins.

Three-wire mode on DO, DI and USCK. DO takes over its PORTA bit while DDRA still sets its direction; as an input, its pull-up follows PORTA. DI and USCK leave port operation alone. As master, software makes the clock by toggling PORTA with the pin an output, for example through USITC.

Two-wire mode on SDA (DI) and SCL (USCK), both bidirectional open-collector, enabled through their DDRA bits. SDA is pulled low when USIDR's output or its PORTA bit is 0, otherwise released. SCL is pulled low when its PORTA bit is 0 or by the start detector, otherwise released; a detected start holds SCL low until USISIF is cleared. Inputs are unaffected; pull-ups on SDA and SCL are off.
Two-wire mode on SDA and SCL as in 0b10, and SCL is also held low after a counter overflow until USIOIF is cleared.

fields.name: USICS
fields.text: Clock source for USIDR and the counter. With the external clock USCK/SCL, the output latch changes the output on the edge opposite the one sampling DI/SDA; with software strobe or Timer/Counter0 compare match the latch is transparent and the output changes at once. 00 selects the software strobe, clocked by writing USICLK 1. With USICS1 1, USICLK chooses between external clocking and USITC software clocking of the counter.

fields.name: USICLK
fields.text: With USICS[1:0] 0, writing 1 shifts USIDR one step and counts the counter up by one in the same instruction cycle, shifting in the value sampled the cycle before. With an external source (USICS1 1) it instead selects USITC as the counter's clock. Reads 0.

fields.name: USITC
fields.text: Writing 1 flips the USCK/SCL output level, whatever the data direction; DDB2 must be 1 for the pin to show it. With USICS1 1 and USICLK 1, a write here clocks the 4-bit counter directly. Reads 0.

fields.name: USIPOS
fields.text: Moves the USI pins: 0 puts them on PB[2:0], 1 on PA[2:0].

registers.name: ACSRA
registers.title: Analog Comparator Control and Status Register A
notes: Initial value of bit 5 printed as N/A.
The settings of ACME are carried on ACSRB.ACM, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: ACD
fields.text: 1 powers the analog comparator off, at any time, saving power in Active and Idle. Clear ACIE before changing it, or the change can raise an interrupt.

fields.name: ACBG
fields.text: 1 puts the internal 1.1 V reference on the comparator's positive input, the reference chosen by REFS[2:0] in ADCSRB and ADMUX; 0 applies AIN0, AIN1 or AIN2 there, as ACM[2:0] choose.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: The comparator output, synchronized and delayed by 1 to 2 clock cycles.

fields.name: ACI
fields.text: Hardware sets it when the comparator output does what ACIS1 and ACIS0 select. With ACIE and SREG.I at 1 the comparator interrupt runs. Cleared when its vector runs or by writing 1 to it.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, 1 enables the analog comparator interrupt; 0 disables it.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: 1, with the ADC off (ADCSRA.ADEN 0), lets the ADC multiplexer choose the comparator's negative input; 0 applies AIN1 there.

fields.name: ACIS
fields.text: Chooses the comparator events that raise the interrupt. Clear the interrupt enable before changing these bits, or the change can raise an interrupt.

registers.name: ACSRB
registers.title: Analog Comparator Control and Status Register B
notes: Initial value of bit 5 printed as N/A.

fields.name: HSEL
fields.text: 1 switches on comparator hysteresis; HLEV sets its level.

fields.name: HLEV
fields.text: With HSEL 1, picks the hysteresis level: 0 for 20 mV, 1 for 50 mV.

fields.name: ACM
fields.text: Chooses the pins on the comparator's positive and negative inputs.

fields.name: ADC6D
fields.text: 1 disconnects the digital input buffer of pin ADC6, and its PIN bit then always reads 0; doing so while the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused saves power in the buffer.

registers.name: ADCSRA
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register A

fields.name: ADEN
fields.text: 1 turns the ADC on, 0 off; turning it off mid-conversion ends that conversion.

fields.name: ADSC
fields.text: Write 1 to start a conversion, each one in Single Conversion mode, the first one in Free Running mode. The first conversion after enabling the ADC, or started together with enabling it, takes 25 ADC clocks instead of 13 and initialises the ADC. Reads 1 while a conversion runs and 0 when done; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ADATE
fields.text: 1 enables auto triggering: a rising edge of the trigger chosen by ADCSRB.ADTS starts a conversion.

fields.name: ADIF
fields.text: Set when a conversion finishes and the data registers are updated. With ADIE and SREG.I at 1 the Conversion Complete interrupt runs. Cleared when its vector runs or by writing 1 to it; a read-modify-write of ADCSRA, SBI and CBI included, can clear a pending interrupt.

fields.name: ADIE
fields.text: With SREG.I also 1, 1 enables the ADC Conversion Complete interrupt.

fields.name: ADPS
fields.text: Divider from the system clock to the ADC clock.

fields.name: ADC9
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 9.

fields.name: ADC8
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 8.

fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 9.

fields.name: REFS
fields.text: With ADCSRB.REFS2, choose the ADC voltage reference. A change during a conversion waits until it ends (ADIF set), and the next conversion takes 25 ADC clocks. A differential input stage can take a while to settle, so after a change either force a long conversion (ADC off, change the reference, ADC on) or discard the first results. An external AREF above VCC - 1 V on channels with differential gain degrades accuracy; internal references cannot be used while an external voltage is on AREF.

rows: External voltage on AREF, internal reference off
Internal 2.56 V (VCC > 3.0 V), no bypass capacitor, AREF disconnected
Internal 2.56 V (VCC > 3.0 V), bypass capacitor on AREF; no external voltage on that pin

fields.name: ADLAR
fields.text: 1 left-adjusts the conversion result in the ADC data register, 0 right-adjusts it; the change applies at once, even mid-conversion.

fields.name: MUX
fields.text: With ADCSRB.MUX5, choose which analog inputs reach the ADC and, for differential inputs, the gain. The same pin on both differential inputs measures offset; single-ended ADC11 selects the temperature sensor. A change during a conversion waits until it ends (ADIF set). After switching to the internal reference the ADC, kept enabled, needs 1 ms to settle; conversions started sooner may be unreliable.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B
notes: The settings of REFS2 are carried on ADMUX.REFS, which holds the low bits.
The settings of MUX5 are carried on ADMUX.MUX, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: BIN
fields.text: Gain stage mode: 0 unipolar (default), one-sided conversions only, the positive input above the negative or the result saturates to the reference, 10-bit result; 1 bipolar, two-sided conversions as two's complement, 9 bits plus sign.

fields.name: GSEL
fields.text: 1 selects 32x gain in place of 20x, and 8x in place of 1x.

fields.name: REFS2
fields.text: Top reference selection bit, choosing between 1.1 V and 2.56 V. With active channels, AVCC or an external AREF above AVCC - 1 V degrades ADC accuracy.

fields.name: MUX5
fields.text: Most significant bit of the channel and gain selection. A change during a conversion waits until it ends (ADIF set).

fields.name: ADTS
fields.text: With ADCSRA.ADATE 1, chooses the source whose interrupt flag's rising edge starts a conversion; with ADATE 0 it has no effect. Switching from a cleared source to a set one makes a rising edge, which starts a conversion if ADEN is 1; switching to Free Running (0) makes no trigger, even with ADIF set.

fields.name: DWDR
fields.text: debugWIRE Data Register.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: CTPB
fields.text: Writing 1 while the temporary page buffer is being filled empties the buffer, losing its data.

fields.name: RFLB
fields.text: With RFLB and SPMEN set, an LPM within three cycles reads the Lock bits or the Fuse bits, as Z0 selects, into its destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles write the temporary buffer to the page addressed by the high part of Z; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the write finishes or if no SPM comes within four cycles. The CPU halts for the whole write.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles erase the page addressed by the high part of Z; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the erase finishes or if no SPM comes within four cycles. The CPU halts for the whole operation.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Enables SPM for the next four clock cycles. Together with CTPB, RFLB, PGWRT or PGERS it gives SPM that bit's meaning; alone, SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z address, ignoring Z's LSB. Clears itself when SPM completes or if none comes within four cycles; stays 1 through a page erase or write. Any low-five-bit value other than 10001, 01001, 00101, 00011 or 00001 does nothing.
